newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 22.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Pakistani newspapers on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- Mir Murtaza Bhutto, 42, chairman of the splinter Shaheed Bhutto group of the Pakistan People's Party, was laid to rest at his ancestral graveyard at Ghari Khuda Baksh amid wailing and weeping crowds of several thousands who attended his last rites.
- President Farooq Leghari filed a reference in the Supreme Court asking it whether or not he could appoint judges to the superior courts without the advice of the prime minister.

- Opposition leader Nawaz Sharif said in the National Assembly (lower house) on Saturday that the killing of Murtaza Bhutto was a direct consequence of a policy of "state terrorism" that he alleged was being pursued by Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government.

- Complete strike was observed in several towns of the southern province of Sindh and all Sindhi-speaking localities of Hyderabad city to protest at the killings of Murtaza Bhutto and his six companions in a shootout with police in Karachi on Friday.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- Iran has prepared a fresh estimate of a gas pipeline that will supply 1,600 million cubic feet per day to Pakistan by the year 1999. The new estimate puts the cost at $10.361 billion, up by $2.0 billion from the last estimate.

- The Asian Development Bank is preparing a long-term policy framework paper for the socio-economic development, trade liberalisation, export expansion, technological growth and industrialisation for Pakistan for up to the year 2010, Commerce Ministry officials said.
- A calamitous situation is emerging in large cotton-growing areas in Punjab province that may hit the cotton ouput.
FINANCIAL POST

- Sources in the State (central) Bank of Pakistan said $200 million has been withdrawn by individuals from foreign currency bank accounts and have sent the cash abroad. They said account holders were unsure of the government's future policy regarding foreign currency accounts.
THE NEWS
- Ukraine has provided its central bank's guarantee against the 15 percent down payment that Pakistan was to release before October 15 for the purchase of 320 main battle tanks worth $550 million.
- The Central Board of Revenue has said it will not extend the last date for sales tax registration fixed as September 30.
- A private sector Pakistani company has expressed willingness to collaborate with Iran for assembly-cum-manufacture of shuttleless looms.

- The Pakistani government's Privatisation Division has sought advice from reputed investment banks and consortia for the sale of three state-owned heavy industrial units -- Heavy Mechanical Complex, Heavy Electrical Complex and Pakistan Engineering Company.
- Pakistan will import 200,000 tonnes of soft white wheat from the United States under the Export Credit Guarantee Programme.
THE NATION

- Nusrat Bhutto, mother of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, has threatened to register cases against her daughter and son-in-law Asif Ali Zardari for the "murder" of Murtaza Bhutto if she did not get justice.
- Pakistan Banking Council chairman Mohammad Ahsan has said the government is keen to revive sick units for generating employment opportunities.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
